mainTopic: The סנדל's twin and birth order, the שליא that makes a house טמא, and the list of five things measured by a טפח
overview: Just before this amud, the גמרא taught that a סנדל (a flattened fetus) is always born with a full twin. So why do the משניות in בכורות and כריתות teach laws about the סנדל itself? The גמרא answers with cases where the twin cannot decide the law: the סנדל is born first (בכורות), the twin is born by caesarean section, or the twin is born before the mother converts (כריתות). The חכמים ask whether the two can even be born at different times, since a ברייתא says they come out wrapped together. רב פפא and רבא each explain how one can still come out first, depending on whether the babies come head first or feet first. Then a new משנה teaches that a שליא (afterbirth) in a house makes the house טמא, because there is no שליא without a baby, while רבי שמעון says the baby dissolved before it came out. The גמרא describes what a שליא looks like and brings a list of five things whose minimum size is a טפח. It then defends that list against other טפח rules, and the amud ends in the middle of another such challenge, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the משנה in בכורות need to mention the sandal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the סנדל law in מסכת בכורות makes, since a סנדל always has a twin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The סנדל that we learned about regarding firstborns: what law is it needed for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה in בכורות teaches a law about a סנדל at all. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in בכורות says the son born after a סנדל is a בכור for inheritance but not for redemption by a כהן. But a סנדל always comes with a full twin, so the twin should already free any later son from פדיון הבן. The סנדל seems to add nothing, so the גמרא asks where it makes a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: A flattened, fish-shaped fetus, often formed when a twin presses on it in the womb
Firstborns; also the name of the מסכת that deals with them
For what law is this needed? (What practical difference does it make?)
Regarding, in the context of

steps.confusionAlert: The question only makes sense if you remember the point made right before: a סנדל never comes alone, there is always a full twin with it. That is why its own law seems useless.

phrases.english: [The sandal that we learned] regarding firstborns,
for what law is it needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the earlier statement on the daf that a סנדל is always born with a twin, and applies that idea to the משנה in בכורות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical case makes the סנדל law in בכורות necessary, given that it always has a twin?

steps.title: The sandal matters when the twin comes out after it
steps.stepSummary: The law matters when the סנדל is born first and the twin afterward. The twin is then a בכור for inheritance but not for פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for the twin that comes after it. That twin is a firstborn for inheritance, but not a firstborn for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the סנדל law matters when the סנדל comes out first and its twin comes out second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the twin came out first, the twin would decide everything and the סנדל would not matter. But when the סנדל comes out first, it already opened the womb, so the full twin after it is not a בכור for redemption by a כהן. Still, the סנדל is not a real viable son, so the twin counts as the firstborn for a double share of inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: For the one who comes after it
A firstborn for inheritance, who receives a double share
A firstborn who must be redeemed from a כהן (פדיון הבן)

steps.whatToRemember: A סנדל born first takes away the twin's status as a בכור לכהן, but not his status as a בכור לנחלה.

phrases.english: For the one that comes after it:
phrases.notes: He means the full twin, born after the סנדל.

phrases.english: he is a firstborn for inheritance,
but he is not a firstborn for the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by pointing to a case where the order of birth makes the סנדל matter.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The law applies when the סנדל is born first: the twin after it is a בכור for inheritance but not for פדיון הבן.

steps.title: Why does the משנה in כריתות need to mention the sandal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the משנה in כריתות, which says a woman who gives birth to a סנדל brings a birth-קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The סנדל that we learned about in כריתות: what law is it needed for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question about a second משנה, in מסכת כריתות. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in כריתות says a woman who gives birth to a סנדל must bring the קרבן of a woman after childbirth. But since there is always a full twin, she would bring that קרבן because of the twin anyway. So the גמרא asks what the סנדל adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The מסכת that deals with כרת and the קרבנות one must bring, including a woman's birth-offering
The offering a woman brings after giving birth

phrases.english: The sandal that we learned regarding Keritot,
for what law is it needed?

steps.triggerLanguage: סַנְדָּל דִּתְנַן גַּבֵּי כָּרֵיתוֹת, לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question as step 1, now aimed at a different משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical case makes the סנדל law in כריתות necessary, if the twin already requires a birth-קרבן?

steps.title: The sandal matters when the twin is born by caesarean section
steps.stepSummary: If the full twin is born by caesarean section and the סנדל comes out through the womb, the mother brings a קרבן because of the סנדל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she gives birth to a baby through the side (caesarean) and to a סנדל through the womb, she brings a קרבן for the סנדל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the סנדל law matters when the full twin is born by caesarean section and only the סנדל is born the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman does not bring a birth-קרבן for a baby born by caesarean section (יוצא דופן). So in this case the full twin creates no obligation at all. The סנדל, which came out through the womb, is what obligates her to bring the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Through the side: a caesarean birth
Through the womb: a normal birth
That she brings an offering

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers follow the same pattern. The סנדל law matters only when the twin cannot set the law, either because it came second (בכורות) or because it was born by caesarean section (כריתות).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a law that seems useless can matter in an unusual case. It also teaches that a caesarean birth does not obligate a birth-קרבן.

phrases.english: That if she gives birth to a child through the side,
and to a sandal through the womb,
she brings an offering for the sandal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 with a case where the twin creates no obligation, so the סנדל alone makes the difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the twin is born by caesarean section and the סנדל through the womb, the mother brings a birth-קרבן because of the סנדל.

steps.title: The caesarean answer does not work for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון, a caesarean baby counts as a real birth, so the mother already brings a קרבן for the twin. The סנדל rule would then add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי שמעון, who says a baby born by caesarean is a full birth, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 4. That answer only works for those who say a caesarean birth does not obligate a קרבן, and רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 needed the twin's birth to be one that does not create a קרבן obligation. For רבי שמעון, a caesarean birth does create the obligation. So in that case the mother brings a קרבן because of the twin anyway, and the סנדל makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby delivered through the side of the mother, by caesarean section
A full, proper offspring that counts as a real birth
What is there to say? A question showing that the earlier answer does not fit this opinion

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Shimon, who said:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצֵא דֶּרֶךְ דּוֹפֶן וָלָד מְעַלְּיָא הוּא
phrases.english: one born through caesarean section is a full-fledged offspring
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: For him the mother already brings a קרבן because of the caesarean twin, so why would the סנדל matter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case given in step 4, according to the opinion of רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי שמעון a caesarean birth already obligates a קרבן, so the סנדל adds nothing new

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the mother converts between the two births
steps.stepSummary: The twin is born while the mother is still a non-Jew, and the סנדל is born after she converts. Only the סנדל's birth obligates her in a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: if she gave birth to the full baby while she was a non-Jew, and to the סנדל after she converted, she brings a קרבן because of the סנדל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a new case that works even for רבי שמעון. The twin's birth does not count because the mother was not Jewish yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a caesarean birth, the twin's birth is excluded here because it happened before the conversion. After she converts, the only birth left is the סנדל. So the משנה in כריתות teaches that a סנדל alone is enough to obligate her in a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The state of being a non-Jew, before converting
She converted and became Jewish
The קרבן a woman brings after giving birth

steps.whyThisMatters: Notice the pattern: each answer looks for a way to cancel the twin's birth so the סנדל stands alone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
That if she gives birth to the offspring while she is a gentile,
and to the sandal after she converted,
she brings an offering for the sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: שֶׁאִם תֵּלֵד וָלָד בְּגַיּוּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 with a new case that works for רבי שמעון
steps.terutzResolutionType: New case (אוקימתא) where the twin's birth does not obligate a קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only way to make the סנדל matter is a caesarean twin, which fails for רבי שמעון
steps.terutzMaskana: A twin born before the conversion does not count, so the סנדל born after the conversion creates the obligation

steps.title: Can the two babies be born separately at all?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב פפא whether these answers are even possible. A ברייתא says the סנדל and its twin always come out wrapped together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said this before רב פפא and asked: are these answers really possible? A ברייתא teaches that when they come out, they come out only wrapped together!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge the answers that depend on the סנדל and the twin being born at different times: the בכורות answer in step 2 and רבי ירמיה's answer in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every answer needed one baby to come out before the other: the סנדל first for בכורות, or the twin first for כריתות. But if the two always come out wrapped together, it seems neither one can be first. That would knock out all the answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Answers, explanations offered to solve a difficulty
Wrapped together, attached to each other
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not only against רבי ירמיה. It challenges every answer that had the two babies born one after the other.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Pappa,
and are these answers really possible?
phrases.notes: He means all the answers above, which needed one baby born before the other.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
when they come out,
they come out only wrapped together!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיתַנְהוּ לְהָנֵי שִׁינּוּיֵי? וְהָא תַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basic assumption behind all the earlier answers
steps.kashyaTarget: All the answers that had the סנדל and twin born at different times (steps 2, 4, 6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the two always come out wrapped together, so it seems impossible for one to be born before the other

steps.title: רב פפא: how the two babies are wrapped
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the twin presses against the middle of the סנדל and pushes it toward the twin's head. They are attached, but not side by side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: learn from this that the baby is wrapped against the סנדל at its middle, and pushes it toward its own head.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא accepts the ברייתא but explains exactly how the babies are wrapped. This sets up his answer for how one can still come out first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean the two lie evenly side by side. The twin's head presses into the middle of the סנדל, so the סנדל sits on the side of the twin's head. That means one baby can lead even though they are attached.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can deduce from here
At its middle, at half its height
Pushes or slides it along
Toward its head

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Learn from this,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְרַךְ כָּרֵיךְ לֵיהּ וָלָד לְסַנְדָּל אַפַּלְגֵיהּ,
phrases.english: the offspring presses against the sandal at its middle,
and pushes it toward its head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by explaining what 'wrapped together' really means
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא: wrapped, but in a way where one baby still leads
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wrapped together means they come out at the same moment
steps.terutzMaskana: They are attached, but the סנדל sits toward the twin's head, so their order depends on how they come out

steps.title: Head-first fits בכורות, feet-first fits כריתות
steps.stepSummary: When the babies come out head first, the סנדל comes out first, which fits the בכורות case. When they come out feet first, the full baby comes out first, which fits the כריתות case.
steps.simpleTranslation: For בכורות, it is where they came out head first, so the סנדל comes out first. For כריתות, it is where they came out feet first, so the full baby comes out first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his answer by using the wrapping to explain both משניות. The direction of the birth decides which baby comes out first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the סנדל sits by the twin's head, a head-first birth brings the סנדל out first. That gives the case from step 2. A feet-first birth brings the full twin out first, which רבי ירמיה's conversion case in step 6 needs. So the answers that depend on birth order stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Their heads; a head-first birth
Their feet; a feet-first birth
Comes out first

steps.whatToRemember: The סנדל and its twin are born wrapped together, but one still comes out first. Head first: the סנדל is first (בכורות). Feet first: the full baby is first (כריתות).

phrases.english: Regarding Bekhorot,
it is where they came out head first,
so the sandal comes out first.
Regarding Keritot,
it is where they came out feet first,
so the offspring comes out first.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי בְּכוֹרוֹת, כְּגוֹן שֶׁיָּצְאוּ דֶּרֶךְ רָאשֵׁיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב פפא's explanation from step 8 to both משניות
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The order of birth depends on whether the babies come out head first or feet first, so both the בכורות answer and the כריתות answers are possible
steps.terutzMaskana: Head first, the סנדל leads (בכורות). Feet first, the full baby leads (the כריתות case of רבי ירמיה), so the answers that depend on birth order stand.

steps.title: רבא's Different Answer: Side by Side, Cases Flipped
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר תחליפא quotes רבא. The twins can lie exactly side by side, as long as we reverse which type of birth fits which case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר תחליפא said in the name of רבא: You can even say the two babies lie exactly side by side, and just reverse the teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way to answer the ברייתא that says the סנדל and its twin come out wrapped together. This line sets up the answer, and the next two steps spell it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא needed the twin to push the סנדל toward its head. רבא says we don't need that picture at all. The twins can be exactly side by side, and we only need to switch which case goes with head-first and which with feet-first.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly even, lying precisely side by side
Reverse it, flip it around
The teaching or ruling (here, רב פפא's matching of cases)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not rejecting the cases themselves. He keeps both cases, בכורות and כריתות, and only swaps which way of being born fits each one.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Tachlifa said in the name of Rava:
You can even say they lie exactly side by side,
and reverse the teaching.
phrases.notes: He means flip what רב פפא said in Step 9, which births go with בכורות and which with כריתות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the challenge of Step 7, in place of רב פפא's answer in Steps 8-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (switching which birth position goes with each source)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a sideways push, as רב פפא described, could explain how the סנדל and the full baby come out at different times.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if the twins lie exactly side by side, the order of birth depends on whether they come out head first or feet first.

steps.title: Feet First: The סנדל Slides Out First (בכורות)
steps.stepSummary: In the בכורות case the babies came out feet first. The live baby holds back, and the lifeless סנדל slips out ahead of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the case of בכורות, the babies came out feet first. The full baby, which is alive, hangs on and does not come out quickly. The סנדל, which has no life, slides right out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the בכורות case. There the babies came out feet first, so the סנדל is born first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live baby coming feet first gets held up, while the lifeless סנדל slides out easily. That is how the סנדל can come out before its twin, which is exactly the בכורות case.

keyTerms.meaning: Their feet (coming out feet first)
Life, being alive
Hangs on, holds back
Slides, slips out

phrases.english: Regarding בכורות, it is where they came out feet first,
the full baby, which has life,
hangs on and does not come out,
the סנדל, which has no life,
slides and comes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of רבא's reversed reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Physical explanation of the birth order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Babies lying side by side should come out together, so the סנדל could not come out first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Feet first, the lifeless סנדל slides out before the live baby, which fits the בכורות case.

steps.title: Head First: The Full Baby Counts as Born First (כריתות)
steps.stepSummary: In the כריתות case the babies came out head first. A live baby counts as born once its head is out, but a סנדל only counts once most of it is out.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the case of כריתות, the babies came out head first. For the full baby, which is alive, once its head comes out it counts as a birth. The סנדל only counts once most of it comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer with the כריתות case. Head first, the full baby counts as born before the סנדל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if both start coming out together, the legal moment of birth is different for each. The live baby is 'born' as soon as its head is out, but the סנדל needs most of its body out. So the full baby is born first, as the כריתות case requires, with the סנדל born later after the mother converts.

keyTerms.meaning: Their heads (coming out head first)
Birth, in the legal sense
Most of it (the majority of its body)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: feet first, the סנדל physically slides out first (בכורות). Head first, the full baby legally counts as born first, because its head is enough while the סנדל needs most of its body out (כריתות).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'who was born first' can depend on a legal rule about when birth happens, and not only on which baby comes out first physically.

phrases.english: Regarding כריתות, it is where they came out head first,
the full baby, which has life,
once its head comes out, it counts as a birth,
the סנדל, only once most of it comes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's reversed reading with the second case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different legal definitions of the moment of birth
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the twins come out together, the full baby could not be born before the סנדל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The head counts as birth for a live baby, but a סנדל needs most of its body out, so the full baby is born first.

steps.title: משנה: A שליא in a House Makes It טמא
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a שליא (afterbirth) in a house makes the house טמא. This is not because the שליא is a baby, but because a שליא always held a baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a שליא in a house, the house is טמא. This is not because the שליא is a baby. It is because there is no שליא without a baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new משנה about a שליא found in a house. The משנה says the house becomes טמא and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything in the house becomes טמא, as if a dead body were there. The משנה is careful about the reason: the שליא itself is not counted as a baby. But a שליא always had a baby inside it, so we assume a baby's body was present.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה we are learning
Afterbirth, the sac that holds the baby
Ritually impure
A baby, offspring

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה calls the שליא a baby. It says the opposite: the house is טמא only because a baby must have been inside the שליא.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: An afterbirth in the house,
the house is impure,
not because the afterbirth is a baby,
but because there is no afterbirth without a baby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The discussion of the סנדל has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליא in a house makes the house טמא because a שליא always held a baby.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: The Baby Dissolved Before It Came Out
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees. He says the baby dissolved before it came out, so the house is not made טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The baby dissolved before it came out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with the first opinion in the משנה. He agrees a baby was there, but he says it was already gone by the time the שליא came out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion assumes a baby's body came out with the שליא. רבי שמעון says the baby turned to liquid inside the womb before it was born. So there is no body to make the house טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Dissolved, broke down

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The baby dissolved before it came out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: נִימּוֹק הַוָּלָד, עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The baby dissolved before birth, so the שליא does not make the house טמא.

steps.title: ברייתא: What a שליא Looks Like
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing a שליא. It starts thin like a thread, grows as wide as a lupine bean, is hollow like a trumpet, and is at least a טפח long.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A שליא at first looks like a thread of the woof, and at the end it looks like a lupine bean. It is hollow like a trumpet, and no שליא is less than a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by explaining what a שליא actually is. This tells us what object the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives signs for recognizing a שליא. It grows from very thin early in the pregnancy to much wider at the end. It is shaped like a hollow tube and is never shorter than a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The cross-threads in weaving (woof)
A lupine, a kind of bean
A trumpet
A handbreadth, a standard measurement

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught: An afterbirth,
at its start looks like a thread of the woof,
phrases.notes: Early in the pregnancy it is as thin as a weaving thread.

phrases.english: and at its end looks like a lupine bean,
and it is hollow like a trumpet,
and no afterbirth is less than a handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁלְיָא — תְּחִלָּתָהּ דּוֹמָה לְחוּט שֶׁל עֵרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the key term שליא from the משנה in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליא starts thread-thin, ends lupine-wide, is hollow like a trumpet, and is at least a טפח long.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: Like a Rooster's Craw
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a different description. A שליא looks like a rooster's craw, with the thin intestine coming out of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A שליא looks like the craw of roosters, which the small intestine comes out of.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא describes the שליא differently. He compares it to a part of a rooster's digestive system.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a trumpet-shaped tube, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל pictures a pouch with a thin tube coming out of it, like a rooster's craw with its small intestine. It is another way to recognize a שליא.

keyTerms.meaning: The craw (gizzard) of a bird
Roosters, chickens
The thin (small) intestines

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה: a שליא in a house makes it טמא because a שליא always held a baby, while רבי שמעון says the baby dissolved first. The גמרא then describes what a שליא looks like: a hollow tube at least a טפח long, or, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, like a rooster's craw.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel says:
An afterbirth looks like the craw of roosters,
which the small intestines come out of.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שִׁלְיָא דּוֹמֶה לְקוּרְקְבָן שֶׁל תַּרְנְגוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second description of the שליא, different from the first opinion in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליא looks like a rooster's craw with the small intestine coming out of it.

steps.title: A list of five things measured by a טפח
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא lists five things whose minimum size is a טפח: שליא, שופר, שדרה, דופן סוכה, and אזוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught by רבי אושעיא, the youngest of the group of sages: There are five things whose size is a טפח. They are: a שליא, a שופר, the spine of a לולב, the wall of a סוכה, and אזוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The last step said a שליא is a טפח long, so the גמרא brings a list of other things that also use a טפח. This list sets up the next few steps, which explain each item one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five rules from very different parts of הלכה are grouped together only because they share the same measurement. The גמרא will now find the source for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, about the width of four fingers
A minimum size or amount required by הלכה
The spine, meaning the thick central stem of a לולב
A wall of a סוכה
Hyssop, a plant used in some טהרה rituals

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא זְעֵירָא דְמִן חַבְרַיָּא —
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Oshaya, the youngest of the group of sages, said:
There are five things whose measure is a handbreadth,
and these are they: an afterbirth, a shofar,
a spine, the wall of a sukka, and the hyssop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the טפח length of a שליא from step 15 to bring a wider list of things measured by a טפח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five things have a minimum size of a טפח: שליא, שופר, שדרה of a לולב, דופן סוכה, and אזוב.

steps.title: Sources for the שליא and the שופר
steps.stepSummary: The שליא rule is the one already quoted. The שופר rule comes from a ברייתא: it must stick out a טפח on each side of the hand holding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שליא is the case we just said. The שופר comes from a ברייתא: How long must a שופר be? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explained: Long enough that a person can hold it in his hand and it can be seen sticking out on this side and on that side, which comes to a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the list. For the שליא it points back to the ברייתא it already quoted, and for the שופר it quotes a new ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hand holding something is about a טפח wide, so a שופר that shows on both sides of the hand is at least a טפח long. This is a practical way of measuring a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: What we already said
Explained
On this side and on that side

phrases.english: An afterbirth: that is what we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא in step 15, which said a שליא is at least a טפח long.

phrases.english: A shofar: as it is taught in a baraita:
How much is the measure of a shofar?
Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel explained:
Enough that he can hold it in his hand,
and it can be seen on this side and on that side: a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins giving the source for each item in the list from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שופר must be long enough to show on both sides of the hand holding it, which is a טפח.

steps.title: The spine of the לולב must stick out a טפח
steps.stepSummary: The spine of a לולב must stick out at least a טפח above the הדס, based on a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the spine rule? רבי פרנך said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The spine of a לולב must stick out a טפח beyond the הדס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third item, the שדרה. Its source is a statement of an אמורא, not a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לולב is tied together with the הדס. The rule is that the לולב's spine must reach at least a טפח higher than the הדס. Keep in mind that this source is a later sage's statement, because that will matter in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: The palm branch taken on סוכות
Myrtle branch, tied together with the לולב
Sticking out beyond

phrases.english: A spine, what is it?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי פַּרְנָךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Parnakh said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The spine of a lulav must
stick out beyond the myrtle a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the list from step 17 with the third item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spine of a לולב must stick out at least a טפח above the הדס.

steps.title: The third wall of a סוכה can be just a טפח
steps.stepSummary: A סוכה needs two full walls, and the third wall can be as small as a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wall of a סוכה comes from a ברייתא: Two walls must be full and proper, and the third can be even a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the fourth item, the wall of a סוכה, by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two walls must be complete. The third wall only needs to be a טפח wide, but it cannot be any smaller. That is why it belongs in this list of things with a minimum of a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Done properly, meeting the full requirements
The third one
Even

phrases.english: The wall of a sukka: as it is taught in a baraita:
Two walls according to their full law,
and a third, even a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the list from step 17 with the fourth item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה needs two full walls and a third wall of at least a טפח.

steps.title: The אזוב must be a טפח
steps.stepSummary: The אזוב must be at least a טפח long, as רבי חייא taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אזוב comes from what רבי חייא taught: The אזוב must be a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list with the fifth item, the אזוב. The wording "תני" presents it as a ברייתא taught by רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pay attention to the word "דתני". It makes this source sound like a ברייתא, and that small detail will cause a counting problem in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule that the אזוב must be at least a handbreadth
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
A sage from the time of the משנה, whose teachings carry the weight of a ברייתא

phrases.english: Hyssop: as Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
Hyssop, a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the last item in the list from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אזוב must be at least a טפח long.

steps.title: A memory aid: three ברייתות and two statements
steps.stepSummary: שילא taught that of the five טפח rules, three come from ברייתות and two come from statements of later sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said: שילא of כפר תמרתא taught: Three ברייתות and two statements of later sages have a measure of a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a way to remember the five טפח rules by sorting them by the kind of source they come from. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three ברייתות are the שליא, the שופר, and the סוכה wall. The two statements are the לולב spine, from רבי יוחנן, and the אזוב. But in step 21 the אזוב was quoted as a ברייתא, so the count does not seem to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or expounded in public
Here it means ברייתות, teachings from the time of the משנה
Statements of later sages (אמוראים)

steps.confusionAlert: Here "מתניתא" does not mean our משנה. It means ברייתות, the outside teachings from the same period. "שמעתתא" means rulings of the later אמוראים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa said:
Sheila of Kefar Temarta taught:
Three baraitot,
phrases.notes: These are the שליא, the שופר, and the סוכה wall.

phrases.english: and two statements of later sages,
phrases.notes: These are the לולב spine and the אזוב.

phrases.english: their measure is a handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּלָת מַתְנְיָתָא, וְתַרְתֵּי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא, שִׁיעוּרָא טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sorts the five sources just listed into ברייתות and statements of later sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of the five טפח rules, three come from ברייתות and two come from statements of later sages.

steps.title: There is only one statement, not two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that only the לולב rule is a later sage's statement, because the אזוב rule was quoted as a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two statements? There is only one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שילא's count. It points out that only one of the five sources is a later sage's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לולב rule came from רבי יוחנן, so it really is a statement. The אזוב rule was introduced with "תני רבי חייא", which makes it a ברייתא. That gives four ברייתות and one statement, not three and two.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
It is only one

phrases.english: Two? It is one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the count in step 22 using the wording of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: שילא's claim that there are two statements of later sages.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the אזוב rule was quoted with "תני", which marks a ברייתא, only the לולב rule is left as a statement.

steps.title: אביי changes the wording of the אזוב rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי says to read the אזוב source as "אמר רבי חייא", so it becomes רבי חייא's own statement and the count works.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Say instead: רבי חייא said: The אזוב must be a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by changing one word in the אזוב source, from "taught" to "said".
steps.deeperAnalysis: With "אמר" in place of "תני", the אזוב rule is no longer a ברייתא but רבי חייא's own ruling. Now there are three ברייתות and two statements, just as שילא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read it this way

steps.whatToRemember: Five things are measured by a טפח: שליא, שופר, לולב spine, סוכה wall, and אזוב. Three come from ברייתות, and two, the לולב and the אזוב, come from statements of later sages, once we follow אביי's wording.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Say instead: Rabbi Ḥiyya said:
phrases.notes: אביי swaps "תני" (taught) from step 21 for "אמר" (said), so this becomes רבי חייא's own ruling.

phrases.english: Hyssop, a handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֵימָא — אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 23 by changing the wording of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אזוב rule was a ברייתא taught by רבי חייא, so there would be only one statement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אזוב rule is רבי חייא's own statement, so there are two statements and three ברייתות.

steps.title: Isn't a one-טפח cube another case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the list of five: there is also the rule that a space of a טפח by a טפח by a טפח spreads טומאה and blocks it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there really no more? But there is the rule that a space a handbreadth by a handbreadth, a handbreadth high, brings the טומאה and blocks the טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the list of five טפח rules is complete, and points to another rule that also uses a טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A space that is a טפח in every direction counts as an אהל. It spreads טומאה to everything inside it and stops the טומאה from going further. If this counts as a טפח rule, then the list should have six items, not five.

keyTerms.meaning: And are there no more? A challenge to a list that claims to be complete.

keyTerms.term: טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח עַל רוּם טֶפַח
keyTerms.meaning: A space a handbreadth by a handbreadth, a handbreadth high (a cube)
Spreads the טומאה to everything under it
Blocks the טומאה from spreading further

phrases.english: And are there no more?
phrases.notes: He means: are there no other rules that use a טפח, besides the five on the list?

phrases.english: But there is a handbreadth by a handbreadth
with a height of a handbreadth, a square space
it brings the impurity,
phrases.notes: If a dead body is in a space this size, the טומאה spreads to everything inside it.

phrases.english: and it blocks the impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the count of five is settled, the גמרא tests whether the list is complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there are exactly five טפח rules
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טפח cube in the laws of טומאה also uses a טפח measure, so it looks like a sixth case.

steps.title: The list counts only a single טפח, not a cube
steps.stepSummary: The list is about measures of one טפח, not a space measured as טפח by טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said 'a handbreadth'; we did not say 'a handbreadth by a handbreadth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the cube does not belong on the list, because the list only counts plain one-טפח measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five rules each measure a single length of a טפח, like the לולב, the אזוב, or the wall of a סוכה. A space measured in two or three directions is a different kind of measure. So it was never meant to be on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: We were saying (this is what our list was talking about)

phrases.english: We said 'a handbreadth,'
we did not say 'a handbreadth by a handbreadth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: טֶפַח קָאָמְרִינַן, טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח לָא קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the טפח cube.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any rule that uses a טפח should be counted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only single-dimension one-טפח measures are counted. A טפח-by-טפח space is excluded.

steps.title: Isn't the stone sticking out of an oven another case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new challenge: a stone sticking out a טפח from a תנור counts as connected to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the rule of a stone that sticks out from the oven a handbreadth, and from the stove three fingerbreadths: it is connected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to find a sixth טפח rule. This time it is a plain single טפח, so the last answer won't help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone sticking out of a תנור by a טפח is treated as part of the תנור. It works like a handle, so if the תנור becomes טמא, the stone is טמא too. This is a simple one-dimension טפח, so it seems it should be on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: An oven
A stove (smaller cooking range)
Fingerbreadths (a smaller unit than a טפח)
Connected: counts as part of the item for טומאה

phrases.english: But isn't there a stone
that sticks out from the oven a handbreadth,
and from the stove three fingerbreadths —
it is connected!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיכָּא אֶבֶן הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַתַּנּוּר טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge that the 'single טפח only' answer cannot solve.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there are exactly five טפח rules
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The oven stone uses a plain one-טפח measure, so it looks like a sixth case.

steps.title: The list counts only minimum sizes
steps.stepSummary: The list only includes cases where less than a טפח is invalid. With the oven stone, less than a טפח is surely a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we said it, we meant where less than a handbreadth is not fit. But here, all the more so, less than a handbreadth is a handle of the oven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the oven stone does not belong on the list, because there the טפח is not a minimum size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All five rules are minimums: below a טפח, the item doesn't work. For the oven stone, the טפח is the most it can stick out and still count as a handle. Anything shorter is certainly a handle. Since the טפח there is an upper limit, not a minimum, it is a different kind of rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than a טפח
Is not fit (does not work for its purpose)
All the more so
A handle of the oven

steps.whatToRemember: The five טפח rules share two features. Each is a single-dimension measure, and each is a minimum, so anything smaller is invalid. A טפח cube fails the first test, and the oven stone fails the second.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the oven stone needs to be at least a טפח. The טפח there is the upper limit. A shorter stone is even more clearly a handle.

phrases.english: When we said it, it was where
less than a handbreadth is not fit,
but here, all the more so
that less than a handbreadth — it is a handle of the oven.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן הֵיכָא דִּבְצִיר מִטֶּפַח לָא חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the oven-stone challenge, so the count of five stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining what kind of measure the list counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any single-טפח measure belongs on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only minimum measures, where less than a טפח is invalid, are counted. The oven stone's טפח is an upper limit, so it is excluded.

steps.title: Opening another challenge to the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins another challenge to the list of five, saying 'But isn't there...' to introduce a case the list seems to be missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't there also...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting another challenge to the list of five, and the case it is pointing to comes right after this word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oven-stone challenge was just answered. Now the גמרא opens another 'you left something out' question. On its own, this word does not yet name the missing case.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't there? This opens a challenge that points to a case someone seems to have left out.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the full challenge in this one word. It only opens the question, and the case itself comes next.

phrases.english: But isn't there

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the oven-stone challenge was answered in step 28, the גמרא starts another challenge of the same kind.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the list of five laws measured by a טפח is complete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It suggests that another case using a טפח measure exists but was left out of the list. The case is named in the words that follow.
